message.content:
Below is a quick‑look guide to **Canadian “long weekends”** in 2023—days when a statutory holiday lands close enough to a regular weekend that most Canadians will enjoy an uninterrupted stretch of free time.  
(For simplicity I’ve focused on *federal* statutory holidays; provincial variations exist but follow similar patterns.)

| Date | Holiday | How it becomes a long weekend |
|------|---------|--------------------------------|
| **January 1–2, 2023** | New Year’s Day (observed Mon Jan 2 after falling on Sunday) | Weekend (Sat Jan 1 & Sun Jan 2) + observed holiday Mon Jan 2 → 3‑day break |
| **March 31 2023** | Good Friday | Friday Mar 31 + weekend (Thu 30–Sat 1) → 3‑day break |
| **May 22 2023** | Victoria Day | Falls on Monday → single‑day holiday (no long weekend) |
| **June 19 2023** | National Indigenous Peoples Day (BC, Yukon, Northwest Territories) | Falls on Monday → single‑day holiday |
| **July 1–2, 2023** | Canada Day (observed Sun Jul 2 after falling on Saturday) | Weekend (Sat Jul 1 & Sun Jul 2) + observed holiday Sun Jul 2 → 3‑day break |
| **September 4 2023** | Labour Day | Falls on Monday → single‑day holiday |
| **October 9 2023** | Thanksgiving | Falls on Monday → single‑day holiday |
| **November 11 2023** | Remembrance Day | Falls on Wednesday → typically requires an additional paid leave day to make a long weekend (not automatic) |
| **December 24–27, 2023** | Christmas Day (Dec 25) & Boxing Day (Dec 26) | Christmas on Monday → short break; Boxing Day on Tuesday adds another workday, but together they give a four‑day stretch (Fri 21–Tue 26) if you take the preceding Friday off |

### Quick Takeaway

- **True “automatic” long weekends** (where the holiday itself causes a multi‑day break without needing extra vacation):  
  • New Year’s Day (Sat Jan 1–Mon Jan 2)  
  • Good Friday (Fri Mar 31)  
  • Canada Day (Sat Jul 1–Sun Jul 2)

- **Other holidays** either land on Mondays (single‑day) or require you to request extra leave to extend them into a longer break.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like state‑specific details (e.g., Alberta’s Heritage Days, Saskatchewan’s Summer Solstice celebrations) or help formatting this into your holiday‑planning app!
